chapter_title: The Chapter of the Man who asks: Why [am] I someti

fills.notes: Fits the correspondential opposition to ¶3 where “wicked considerations” disorder doctrines; here the inward “consideration” is formative/ordering.

The sequence demands an adverbial qualifier on the outward works matching the inward order (“doctrines … ordered and in place”). The oldest-layer register prefers an impersonal ethical-structural term (“without fault”) rather than later moralizing; it also balances ¶3 “I shall do … in my works” where the outward becomes disordered.
Direct antithesis to ¶2/¶10: ordered doctrine → confusion; and it anticipates “source of trouble and confusion.”

fills.fill: I may be rid of them
fills.notes: The clause needs an infinitival complement after “I shall not find how …”: inability to expel/subdue the intruding counsels. This matches the earlier struggle “that I would subdue them; not finding the strength…”.
The disturbance is said to enter through multiple correspondential ‘channels’: stars/roots below/above, then later food/water. “Many ways” keeps the impersonal cosmological tone.

Syntax requires a finite verb before “they turn over him and stir him…”. In this substrate, stars ‘rule/turn’ a person by their dominion; “rule him” sets up the subsequent actions (turn, stir, trouble).
The sentence contrasts a tranquil heavenly influx with a sudden intrusion from nourishment; “and then” introduces the reversal demanded by the correspondential logic.
Parallelism with the next clause “or in the water that they have drunk” and later repetition “nourishment of the bread… and the water…”.
Editor fill retained; it matches the ‘mixture’ doctrine: alien troublesome parts are carried in and commingled with bodily parts.
Completes “pure …” with a second purity-term typical of the substrate’s material correspondences (refined/clarified = more Light, less residue).
The “atmosphere above” is calmed by purification of the airs/winds (a standard cosmological conduit). This keeps the upward/downward conduit schema used in ¶11.
The “image” (inner form) is calmed when stirred motions cease; “agitation” corresponds to the turbulent lust/anger listed elsewhere.
What “increases in you through those good parts” is the ordered, luminous faculty named elsewhere: wisdom/true knowledge/Mind in gladness.
Bridges the causal explanation: carefree soul is so “because” of alliance with the living souls present within (light-parts in the pure nourishment).

assessment: Most gaps are constrained by the chapter’s conduit-structure (above/below; stars/roots; food/water) and by the strict opposition between ordered/light states and confused/dark states. Where the Coptic leaves room (¶2 #3; ¶3 #2; ¶10 #1–3, #6), restorations are guided by the oldest-layer correspondential mechanics: inward order expresses itself as faultless outward work; disturbances enter by multiple channels; purification/refinement of nourishment and airs calms the inner image and increases wisdom.
